title: A Personal Brand Is Not an Institution
author: RN Collins
rightsRule: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

carouselA.title: A Personal Brand Is Not an Institution: the institutional sequence

frames.caption: A personal brand makes a person recognizable. An institution makes their judgment, relationships, records, rights, and work capable of operating beyond constant personal performance.
frames.alt: Title plate for A Personal Brand Is Not an Institution.
frames.treatment: typography, rule, folio and domain color only

frames.caption: The house is visible as both maker attribution and an enduring cataloguing unit.
frames.credit: Gift of Mrs. Philip K. Rhinelander, 1946
frames.alt: Elaborately trimmed silk ball gown by the House of Worth, dated around 1872.
frames.treatment: local display and download with attached credit

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 01 · SIGNAL — What does the public recognize?. Identify the repeated promise, visual language, subject, and point of view that make the person legible. These signals matter, but they are evidence of recognition—not proof that the work can be produced, governed, or continued.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what does the public recognize? within A Personal Brand Is Not an Institution.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 02 · SYSTEM — What repeats without performance?. Map how research becomes a brief, how decisions are approved, how work is produced, and how quality is reviewed. A system must be inspectable enough to improve and flexible enough to accommodate judgment.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what repeats without performance? within A Personal Brand Is Not an Institution.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 03 · ASSET — What remains under accountable control?. Separate reputation from the name, entity, marks, domains, mailing list, contracts, files, samples, and archive. The public may perceive one identity while ownership and access are fragmented across many records.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what remains under accountable control? within A Personal Brand Is Not an Institution.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
frames.caption: 04 · ABSENCE — What happens when the founder is offline?. Run a seventy-two-hour absence test. Can collaborators find current files, communicate with clients, fulfill obligations, protect accounts, and identify who may decide? The gaps reveal where a brand still depends on continuous personal availability.
frames.credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
frames.alt: Diagram mapping what happens when the founder is offline? within A Personal Brand Is Not an Institution.
frames.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
frames.treatment: render from verified text, source IDs, lines and geometric fields

frames.caption: Institutionalization can turn a living voice into bureaucracy. The aim is not to make the person interchangeable; it is to protect the conditions that let singular judgment remain singular without making exhaustion the operating model.
frames.alt: Counterpoint card for A Personal Brand Is Not an Institution.
